title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Credit Owed for the Pre-Agreement Inspection on Settlement
content:
## Estimating desk note

A credit is owed, on a settlement of a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record, for the pre-agreement inspection where it has not yet been passed back through a billing adjustment. Two readings decide it: whether any credit has been issued on the agreement as a billing adjustment, and how long ago the agreement was signed.

### The ladder

1. Where the agreement was signed **no more than 12 whole months** before the settlement day and no credit has been issued on it as a billing adjustment, the tier's pre-agreement inspection fee is owed at the recent inspection share, that is 100 percent of the fee.
2. Where the agreement was signed **more than 12 whole months** before the settlement day and no credit has been issued on it as a billing adjustment, the tier's pre-agreement inspection fee is owed at the older inspection share, that is 50 percent of the fee.
3. Where a **credit has been issued** on the agreement as a billing adjustment, no credit is owed for the pre-agreement inspection.

The fee is the pre-agreement inspection fee published for the agreement's tier on the proposal desk sheet; at a tier that requires no pre-agreement inspection that published fee is nothing, so nothing is owed under this note.

### Boundary and cases (hypothetical)

- Signed exactly 12 whole months before the settlement day, with no billing adjustment credit issued: "no more than 12", so the full fee is owed. At 13 whole months, half of it is owed.
- At a tier whose pre-agreement inspection fee is 650.00 USD, signed 4 months ago with no billing adjustment credit: 650.00 USD is owed. Signed 20 months ago on the same facts: 325.00 USD.
- Where any credit has been issued on the agreement as a billing adjustment, neither share applies and nothing is owed.
